findings.location: Methods p.5 vs Supplementary Data 1 sheet 'Table 2'
findings.evidence: Methods p.5: 'the final cutoff being 0.6, meaning that samples were predicted as negative, if a probability of more than 60% was determined'. Table 2 CarbaDetector column (TP 230, TN 125, FP 22, FN 8) is identical to the 'random forest expanded sensitive' column of Supplementary Data 1 sheet 'Table 2' (230/125/22/8), so the stored predictions are the ones behind the table; the direction of the 0.6 rule (negative if p>0.6) is the opposite of the stated aim of raising sensitivity and is not verifiable without the code.
findings.question_for_authors: Does the 0.6 cut-off classify p>0.6 as negative or as positive, and which column of Supplementary Data 1 holds the CarbaDetector predictions?
